To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) NIR light can be transmitted through human head tissues, (ii) the spatial arrangement of NIR light emitters has a negligible influence on NIR light penetration through human head tissues and (iii) NIR light can penetrate through human head tissues without causing thermal effects to the brain.

(a) finite element analysis of photon diffusion in a 3D human model shows that NIR light emitted from an LED array produces an illumination field that is radially symmetric, (b) measurement of transcranially transmitted NIR light in cadaveric human tissues confirms that NIR light emitted by the LED array closely matches simulation results, and (c) NIR illumination of the brain with the LED array does not cause thermal damage to brain tissues.

the simulation of photon propagation in a 3D human model shows that LED emitters in a quasi-radially distributed array can produce a quasi-radially symmetric illumination field, and measurements on excised cadaveric human tissues show that the illumination of NIR light with an LED array produces a photon flux that follows the simulation results.
